what: Image Compare finds the differences between two versions of a picture. It compares them pixel by pixel, colours every changed pixel, and tells you how many pixels changed and what percentage of the image that is.

Switch between four views: a highlight view with changes in a bright colour, a slider that wipes between the two images, side by side, and a difference map that shows how strong each change is. A threshold lets you ignore tiny differences such as JPG compression noise.
Both images are compared in your browser and never uploaded.
uses: Compare website or app screenshots before and after a code change to catch layout bugs.
See exactly what changed between two versions of a design or banner.
Find the hidden changes in puzzle pictures in seconds.
Check what a retouch, filter or compression actually changed.
Compare scans or exports of the same page.
tutorial: Click or drop the original picture on the box marked Image A.
Do the same with the changed picture. You can also drop both files on one box at once.
The tiles show the percentage of different pixels, the number of changed pixels and the size used to compare them.
Raise the threshold to hide tiny colour changes. Around 10% hides most compression noise; 0% counts every change.
Highlight colours changed pixels; Slider lets you drag between A and B; Side by side shows both; Difference only shows the strength of each change.
If the images are different sizes, choose to stretch B to A or line up the top-left corners.
Press "Download this view (PNG)" to save what you see.
features: Every pixel is checked, including transparency.
Know how big a change is at a glance.
Ignore noise from compression or resizing.
Highlight, wipe slider, side by side and difference map.
Stretch or align images that are not the same size.

example.title: Worked example: checking a website change
example.text: A developer takes a screenshot of the home page before and after updating the page styles. She drops both screenshots in. The tool reports 1.8% different pixels and the Highlight view shows red only around the buttons, which is what she changed, plus a small red line in the footer she did not expect. She uses the Slider to look closer, finds a spacing bug in the footer and fixes it before release.

tips: Compare images of the same size for the most accurate result.
Use PNG screenshots when possible; JPG adds small differences everywhere.
Start with a 10% threshold and lower it if you suspect subtle colour changes.
Use the Slider view to judge whether a change matters visually.
Swap A and B if you dropped them the wrong way round.
problems: The images may be shifted by a few pixels or have different sizes. Make sure both screenshots show exactly the same area.
This is usually JPG compression. Raise the threshold.
A very large image was scaled down
Images over about 16 megapixels are scaled down to compare them. Crop them to the area you care about for full detail.
